# Databricks Meeting Briefing: 17 November 2026

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This briefing covers Databricks activity from roughly 16 October to 15 November 2026, the 30 days before the meeting. It draws on Databricks' release notes for Google Cloud, AWS, and Azure, Databricks Community posts, Microsoft Learn, a Fundz product-launch page, and secondary reporting from SaaS deal trackers and Wikipedia. Items that could not be verified against a primary Databricks source are flagged in Section 8.

## 2. Executive Summary

- **Genie One is now distributed beyond Databricks' own interfaces.** Between 10 and 11 November 2026, Databricks shipped connectors or plugins linking Genie One to ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor/Grok Bot, and Microsoft 365 Copilot, plus a Chrome extension and a Windows desktop app ([Databricks, 2026a](https://docs.databricks.com/gcp/fr/release-notes/product/2026/november); [Microsoft, 2026](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/release-notes/product/2026/november)).
- **Enterprise governance features were a major theme.** Changes included partner-platform ingress rules, budget webhooks, and Unity Catalog wikis ([Databricks, 2026a](https://docs.databricks.com/gcp/fr/release-notes/product/2026/november); [Microsoft, 2026](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/release-notes/product/2026/november)).
- **Two near-term changes carry operational risk.** The Genie One MCP Beta endpoint ends on 30 November 2026, and variant shredding becomes default on new tables on 18 November 2026 with a breaking change for Databricks Runtime 15.4 ([Microsoft, 2026b](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/release-notes/whats-coming)).
- **No verified acquisitions, funding rounds, or executive hires fall within the 30-day window.** The most recent verified deal, the Row Zero acquisition, was announced on 24 September 2026 ([SaaSRise, 2026](https://www.saasrise.com/deals/databricks-buys-row-zero-and-is-scouting-for-more-startups-to-acquire-0cf62ecf-edbc-447c-934d-7ef5822b8bd5)).

## 3. Product and Platform Changes (Last 30 Days)

The table below lists the main verified changes in the window. Dates are as stated in the release notes.

| Date (2026) | Change | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Nov | AI Functions usage (e.g., `ai_parse_document`, `ai_extract`, `ai_classify`) counts toward Unity Gateway budgets | Generally available | [Microsoft, 2026](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/release-notes/product/2026/november) |
| 2 Nov | `ai_decide` moves to a new model, reported as 33% more accurate with unchanged latency | Beta | [Microsoft, 2026](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/release-notes/product/2026/november) |

### Analyst Observations

The November releases form a coherent pattern. Databricks is pushing Genie One out of its own UI and into the assistants enterprises already use, including ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Cursor, Slack, and Chrome. The governance features (ingress rules for partner platforms, budget webhooks, and access modes) appear designed to answer the obvious enterprise objection: that expanded access creates control and cost exposure. The release notes show the governance layer keeping pace with the distribution layer, but the sources do not show usage, adoption, or pricing data to confirm whether customers are adopting these surfaces at scale.

## 4. Genie One Ecosystem Expansion

The most significant cluster of announcements falls on 11 November 2026. Verified items include:

- **ChatGPT.** A ChatGPT admin sets up the Databricks Genie plugin for the workspace, and each user signs in with a Databricks account ([Databricks, 2026a](https://docs.databricks.com/gcp/fr/release-notes/product/2026/november)).
- **Claude.** A Claude admin connects the Databricks Genie connector for the team ([Databricks, 2026a](https://docs.databricks.com/gcp/fr/release-notes/product/2026/november)).
- **Cursor and Grok Bot.** A Cursor team admin publishes the plugin for the team ([Microsoft, 2026](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/release-notes/product/2026/november)).
- **Microsoft 365 Copilot.** The Azure Databricks Genie plugin for Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat is in Public Preview, allowing questions without an @-mention ([Microsoft, 2026](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/release-notes/product/2026/november)).
- **Microsoft Copilot Cowork.** A Public Preview plugin that requires no OAuth app or manifest edits. Existing Beta manifest-based installations are not migrated automatically ([Microsoft, 2026](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/release-notes/product/2026/november)).

Genie Search, now generally available, indexes content from Google Drive, Jira, Confluence, and Workday, and preserves source-system permissions ([Databricks, 2026b](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/november)).

## 5. Governance, Security, and Platform Operations

- **Partner-platform ingress.** Databricks maintains the published IP ranges of ChatGPT and Claude, so customers do not track them manually ([Databricks, 2026a](https://docs.databricks.com/gcp/fr/release-notes/product/2026/november)).
- **Budget governance.** AI Functions spend is included in Unity Gateway budgets from 1 November, and budget events can now trigger webhooks for incident and ticketing workflows ([Microsoft, 2026](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/release-notes/product/2026/november)).
- **Compliance-profile defaults.** Several features are moving to default-on for compliance-profile workspaces, including Feature Views, Genie file upload from 15 November, and Genie Code tasks in Lakeflow Jobs ([Microsoft, 2026](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/release-notes/product/2026/november); [Microsoft, 2026b](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/release-notes/whats-coming)).
- **Model access.** Gemini 4 Carbon is available through Unity Gateway. Databricks states that customers are responsible for ensuring their own compliance with applicable terms ([Databricks, 2026b](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/november)).

## 6. Deals, Partnerships, and Corporate Activity

### Acquisitions and Funding

No acquisition or funding event is verified within the 30-day window. The most recent verified transactions are:

| Date | Event | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 24 Sep 2026 | Acquired Row Zero (spreadsheet tool); terms undisclosed. CEO Ali Ghodsi reportedly said more acquisitions are planned | [SaaSRise, 2026](https://www.saasrise.com/deals/databricks-buys-row-zero-and-is-scouting-for-more-startups-to-acquire-0cf62ecf-edbc-447c-934d-7ef5822b8bd5) |
| 12 Aug 2026 | Acquired Electric (PGlite team) | [Tracxn, 2026](https://tracxn.com/d/acquisitions/acquisitions-by-databricks/__h71WlGEvmuefCzSdZogxaGihmuCYu0rBKj3hkmJQF7M) |
| 3 Aug 2026 | Completed acquisition of Panther | [Telosi, 2026](https://telosi.io/vr/databricks) |
| 13 Aug 2026 | Closed a $5 billion round at a $190 billion valuation, as stated in the company's release | [Telosi, 2026](https://telosi.io/vr/databricks) |

Tracxn records 23 total acquisitions, six of them in 2026 ([Tracxn, 2026](https://tracxn.com/d/acquisitions/acquisitions-by-databricks/__h71WlGEvmuefCzSdZogxaGihmuCYu0rBKj3hkmJQF7M)). Acquisition price data for most deals is not disclosed.

### Partnerships

Wikipedia reports an expanded Databricks–Microsoft partnership announced in July 2026, covering mutual product integration and Genie's presence in Microsoft 365, Teams, and Copilot ([Wikipedia, 2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Databricks)). This predates the window. The November Microsoft-related plugin launches are the in-window expression of that partnership. The Wikipedia entry is a secondary source, and the primary July announcement was not in the materials reviewed.

## 7. Executive and Key Hires

No executive or key hire is verified within the window. The most recent entry in the available timeline is Simon Davies' appointment as SVP and GM for Asia Pacific and Japan on 20 April 2026 ([Telosi, 2026](https://telosi.io/vr/databricks)). This is well outside the window, and the timeline is a third-party compilation.

## 8. Verification Flags and Source Reliability

| Item | Issue | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Fundz "second-generation Genie" launch (11 Nov 2026) | Stated by a sales-intelligence vendor. No corresponding Databricks release note was found in the materials. Fundz also has a commercial interest in promoting launch alerts | **Unverified.** Confirm with Databricks |
| Gemini 4 Carbon availability | Confirmed in two Databricks release-note sources | Verified |
| Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Cowork plugins | Public Preview status stated by Microsoft Learn | Verified (preview status) |
| YouTube "Databricks Product Announcements in 5 Minutes" | Only page metadata was available; no content | **Not verified** |
| Acquisition multiples and valuations (Tracxn, SaaSRise) | Derived or estimated figures; SaaSRise's "2–3x" premium is speculation | **Not used** |
| Electric acquisition date | Telosi and Tracxn differ by one day (11 vs. 12 August) | Minor discrepancy, not material |
| "New jobs compute defaults to Auto access mode" | Headline only; no detail in the source excerpt | **Partially verified** |
| Wikipedia Microsoft partnership (July 2026) | Secondary source; primary announcement not reviewed | Plausible; treat with caution |

Primary sources (Databricks docs and Microsoft Learn release notes) are the most reliable. Tracxn, Telosi, SaaSRise, and Atlan are third-party trackers and are used only for dates and transaction facts. The Databricks Community posts are company-affiliated but informal.

| 1 Dec 2026 (on or after) | Billing begins for private network gateway usage | Cost | [Microsoft, 2026b](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/release-notes/whats-coming) |
| 1 Feb 2027 | AI Functions requiring Runtime 15.4 LTS+ stop working on runtimes below 17.3 LTS in SQL | Operations | [Microsoft, 2026](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/release-notes/product/2026/november) |

## 10. Analyst Assessment

Based on the verified materials, my view is that the most consequential development in the window is not any single launch but Databricks' decision to make Genie One a cross-platform access layer. Placing Genie inside ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft 365 Copilot, and Cursor widens the surfaces where Databricks data gets queried, which makes the company's position more dependent on the governance layer working reliably. The ingress, budget, and access-control releases in the same weeks suggest Databricks understands that risk.

Two items warrant direct attention in the meeting. First, the Genie One MCP Beta endpoint ends on 30 November, which is two weeks after the meeting. Any customer still on the Beta endpoint will need a migration path, and a Beta-to-GA transition at this point suggests the endpoint change was pulled forward once already (from 31 October). Second, the variant shredding default on 18 November is a breaking change for Runtime 15.4 clusters. If that change is not well communicated, it could generate support load.

The main gap in the record is commercial. The release notes describe a pay-as-you-go model for Genie in a Community article title, but the materials contain no pricing detail, adoption metrics, or customer data. Without those, it is hard to judge whether the November expansion is a meaningful revenue driver or primarily a distribution play.

## 11. Open Questions for Databricks

1. With the Genie One MCP Beta endpoint ending on 30 November 2026, what migration support is available for customers still on the Beta endpoint, and what share of Genie One MCP traffic has already moved to `system.ai.genie_one_mcp`?
2. Genie One can now be reached through ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Slack, Chrome, and Windows. How does Databricks govern usage, cost, and data-access consistency across these surfaces, and how is consumption priced across them?
3. Fundz describes a "second-generation Genie" launched on 11 November 2026. Can Databricks confirm this characterization and explain what changed relative to Genie One, which is already described as generally available?
